title: Fabric Runtime Release Channels
summary: A Fabric Updates Blog announcement introducing Fabric Runtime Release Channels, a mechanism that splits every Spark runtime into a default and an early-access channel so customers can validate upcoming library, dependency, security, and OS updates against their own workloads before those changes become the production default.
audience: Fabric platform admins and Spark/data engineering teams who need a testing window before runtime-level Spark changes reach production notebooks and jobs.
why_it_matters: Runtime updates previously reached production without warning, so teams could be surprised by library or dependency shifts breaking a workload; this gives engineering teams a way to opt in early, test against their own code, and catch incompatibilities before the update becomes mandatory.
takeaways: Every Spark runtime now exposes two channels: a default production channel everyone runs automatically, and an early-access channel with the next set of changes for opt-in testing.
The channel lifecycle is cyclical: publish to early access, customers validate, early access is promoted to the new default, and a fresh early-access channel opens for the next round.
Opting in is two Spark configuration properties set on an Environment item, not a separate infrastructure change, and can be reverted with no permanent effect.
Per-channel release notes and a VHD-version lookup command let teams track exactly what changed between the default and early-access channel.
This is a testing/validation mechanism, not a way to permanently pin an older runtime version.

claims.text: Fabric Runtime Release Channels give customers a validation window for Spark runtime updates -- including library upgrades, dependency changes, security patches, and OS updates -- before those changes reach the production default, addressing prior feedback that updates could disrupt workloads with no warning.

Each Spark runtime now has two channels: a Default channel running the current production-grade runtime automatically for all users, and an Early access channel, also production-grade, containing the next set of updates for customers to test before promotion.

The release channel lifecycle is cyclical: Microsoft publishes upcoming changes to the early-access channel, customers get a validation window to test workloads against it, the early-access channel is then promoted to become the new default, and a fresh early-access channel opens with the next round of changes.

Opting a session into the early-access channel requires setting two Spark configuration properties on an Environment item -- spark.fabric.pools.skipStarterPools=true and spark.computeConf.runtime.releaseChannel=earlyAccess -- then attaching that environment to a notebook or Spark job definition; removing or resetting the setting reverts to default with no permanent change.

Release notes are published separately per channel in a Spark Runtime Releases and Updates repository, letting teams compare default versus early-access notes side by side to see exactly what is coming before it is promoted.

The exact VHD (virtual hard disk) version underlying a running Spark session can be identified by calling spark.conf.get("spark.synapse.vhd.id", "") in that session, giving a precise build identifier beyond just default-versus-early-access.
